analysis:
Examined ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift (head, lines 4-7, 103-128) and ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift (patch hunks near 1133 and 1201; base excerpt only covers up to line 551, so the unload code is seen via the patch only).

Lifecycle change: the drain now waits up to drainReconnectGrace (10s, bounded by finishDeadline) for a registered coordinator connection before sending the drain acknowledgement. If the session is down and unacknowledged, sessionDown=true lets a non-forced drain reach .drained (line 127-128). Security impact: no accepted work is truncated, because the outcome still requires lifecycleRemaining==0 and nativeOwnersDrained, and the disconnect itself already cancelled accepted work. The loop is bounded, honours Task.isCancelled, and does not affect admission: beginServingDrain has already refused new work. Marking drained without a coordinator ack only affects the local lifecycle/stop path. Any residual coordinator-side effect (stale routing/busy view, A-018) depends on coordinator handling, which is out of scope. T-053 stale-authorization concerns are unchanged here, since the App Attest worker is still stopped via stopAppAttestWorkerAndWait before the outcome is set. One caveat: a TOCTOU between the connected check and sessionDown is benign.

Model loading change: selectedModelRecovery.makeAllDue(now:) is called after a successful Nemotron Super retire and after a normal unload. This only reschedules recovery checks for selected models at the next capacity tick. It does not bypass the memory admission, eviction, weight-hash or autopilot ownership gates inside ensureModelLoaded, which I saw in the base text. The unload path does not appear to alter KV-cache purge or SSD-cache semantics (T-041).

Open question for integration: whether makeAllDue could create load churn or availability loops with the add-on hold (TB-012/T-059). The hold path was not in the supplied evidence, so I record it as uncertain rather than as a finding. No concrete security regression identified.
